title: Associate onboarding and interview signal matrix (first 120)
content:
Purpose:
This working doc bundles three pieces we keep iterating on for early-career / associate-level hires: a concise interview signal matrix for quick calibration, an interview scorecard template with anchor language, and a pragmatic first-120-day onboarding checklist that managers and mentors can copy.

Context and constraints:
- Target roles: Associate SWE, Associate SRE, Associate Applied-ML engineer, entry-level Solutions Engineer.
- Hiring cadence: small, sprinty cohorts (2–4 hires / quarter) — we prioritize fast feedback loops and repeatable onboarding templates.
- Audience: hiring managers, interviewers (ICs), recruiters, onboarding buddies.

Quick summary of changes in this draft (what to review):
- Reworked signal matrix into 5 clear competency buckets (Signal/Anti-signal examples).
- Introduced a 1–4 numeric rubric (no zeros) with explicit anchor sentences for each score per competency.
- Condensed manager checklist into weekly themes (week0, week1–4, month2, month3, month4) to reduce checklist fatigue.
- Added hiring timeline suggestions for a 3-week end-to-end loop from screen -> on-site -> offer.

Interview signal matrix (calibration shorthand) — use this at the start of interviewer debriefs:
Competency buckets: Fundamentals, Problem-solving & Communication, System Design (scaled for associate), Ownership & Bias for Action, Team fit & Learning agility.
- Fundamentals (languages, debugging, core CS):
  Strong signal: writes clear, correct code quickly, can reason about complexity, explains tradeoffs.
  Weak/anti-signal: frequent misconceptions about basics (O(N) vs O(N log N)), cannot debug a simple failing test after hints.
- Problem-solving & Communication:
  Strong signal: breaks problem into steps, verbalizes assumptions, adapts when given counterexamples.
  Weak/anti-signal: jumps to code without clarifying input/output or stops after hitting first blocker.
- System Design (entry-level):
  Strong signal: draws small service flow, identifies primary bottleneck, proposes simple mitigation (caching, retry).
  Weak/anti-signal: conflates deployment infra and app logic, proposes heavy infra without tradeoffs.
- Ownership & Bias for Action:
  Strong signal: gives examples of taking small scoped initiatives, shipping incremental improvements.
  Weak/anti-signal: experience limited to shadowing; lacks examples of follow-through.
- Team fit & Learning agility:
  Strong signal: asks about mentorship, demonstrates curiosity, integrates feedback.
  Weak/anti-signal: dismissive of feedback or fixed-view about tooling/languages.

Scorecard rubric (1-4) — use numeric + short note, then overall hire/no-hire recommendation.
- 4 = Exceeds expectations for level; demonstrated in >3 competency buckets with concrete outcomes. Anchor: "Candidate independently owned/led projects or delivered features with measurable impact; clearly can mentor peers in near term."
- 3 = Meets expectations for level; shows independent execution on small-to-medium scoped tasks. Anchor: "Solid fundamentals, reasonable system thinking, clear communicator; will ramp to full ownership in 3–6 months."
- 2 = Borderline; partial signals in multiple buckets but key gaps exist. Anchor: "Needs close mentorship, can contribute after several months; may be appropriate with strong team bandwidth or education plan."
- 1 = Does not meet expectations for level. Anchor: "Significant gaps in fundamentals or problem solving; not recommended for hire at this level."
Notes for interviewers: write one sentence that justifies your numeric score (avoid vague adjectives). Mark any 'must ask' follow-ups for loop coordinator. Add a single line about culture fit (concise).

Interview loop template (fast 3-week flow example) — adjust for recruiter/manager constraints:
Week 0: Recruiter phone screen (30m) => role overview, logistics, salary band, basic culture fit.
Week 1: Technical screen (45m) — coding/debugging; one take-home code challenge optional for SWE shortlist.
Week 2: Round robin loop (3x45m): coding, system-sense + debugging, behavioural/ownership + team fit. Prefer at least two different interviewers for coding/PS.
Week 3: Debrief & offer (recruiter + hiring manager); target 48–72 hour decision window after loop.
Tips: limit onsite to 3 interviews for associates; avoid heavy system design. Provide take-home exercises only when they replace a panel (not in addition).

Hiring plan sprint (recommended channels & timeline):
- Channels: campus / new-grad fairs, targeted bootcamp partners, early-career-referral bonuses, junior-focused job boards, university CS clubs via alumni.
- Role card template: 4–6 bullets focused on day 1–90 deliverables, must-have vs nice-to-have, clear level-up path.
- SLA goals: source shortlist (6–8) within 10 business days; technical screens scheduled within 7 days of application; loop within 7 days of passing screen.
- Offer turnaround: get verbal approval within 48 hours; extend formal offer within 5 business days.

Offer calibration and compensations notes:
- For associates we keep bands tight; include relocation stipend if needed and a small sign-on for high-demand skill paths.
- Include clear career mapping doc with 6-month milestones to reduce early attrition.

First-120-day onboarding checklist (pragmatic manager-ready):
Pre-day0 (recruiter/IT): account/email access, calendar invites, hardware order + VPN/credentials, short welcome note with first-day agenda and reading list.
Week0 (day 0–5) — orientation and context:
- Day0: 1:1 with manager (30m) -> success expectations, first-week goals.
- Day1: team meet-and-greet, role-level doc, repo access, dev environment help session.
- W0 tasks: small 'sandbox' ticket to run the app locally; setup pair session with buddy.
Week1–4 — focused ramping:
- Week1: complete two small tickets (one bugfix, one minor feature) with code review feedback. Weekly sync with manager.
- Week2: ownership of one small service area; demo to team by end of week.
- Week3: rotate on-call shadow or runbook walkthrough (SRE tracks).
- Week4: first retro-style 1:1 reflection with manager + updated development plan.
Month2 (weeks 5–8): take on medium scoped task, lead one small cross-team sync, identify three learning goals.
Month3–4 (weeks 9–16): deliver measurable impact (bug backlog reduction, perf fix, onboarding doc), present to team, calibration check with People Ops on ramp.
Manager checklist items (copy/paste into calendar):
- Weekly 1:1s scheduled for first 12 weeks (30m).
- Pair-programming slots first 4 weeks.
- Midpoint 60-day feedback meeting with written notes.
- End of 120-day review: fill in simple rubric and define next milestones.

Onboarding quick-wins for new hires (to build early confidence):
- Merge a documentation PR within week 1 (even small).
- Fix a flaky test and add a comment.
- Shadow a customer debug call.

Risks & open questions (items to resolve before mass adoption):
- Do we require take-home coding for remote candidates? (pros: more signals; cons: bias/time sink)
- hiring budget for junior sign-on incentives — propose cap per quarter.
- Need better campus pipeline tracking in Greenhouse (ticket: JIRA-OPS-3247).

Appendix: sample short scorecard (paste into Greenhouse comments) — one line per competency + numeric: 
- Fundamentals: 3
- Problem-solving: 3
- System-sense: 2
- Ownership: 3
- Fit/Learning: 4
Overall: 3 -> "Would hire for associate SWE; clear plan for first 90 days to close system-sense gap."

How to use this doc:
- Recruiter: copy loop template & SLA to job posting and scheduling messages.
- Interviewers: use signal matrix before debrief, leave one-line justification for score.
- Managers: copy the first-120 checklist into a new hire onboarding calendar and share with buddy.

Notes to reviewers (open):
- Please add alternate source partners we haven't listed, especially for underrepresented campuses.
- Feedback on the 1–4 scale anchors welcome — aim to finalize for Q2 hiring cohorts.

Track changes log (short):
- 2026-02-08: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2026-02-20: updated rubric anchors (Marisol)
- 2026-03-10: tightened loop timeline and added SLA targets (Ethan)

End of doc.
